newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Biora sets US product launch.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Biora sets US product launch.

text.p: Swedish biotechnology company Biora AB will launch its main product, a treatment for periodontal disease, in the United States April 15, chief executive Tomas Hammargren said on Wednesday.
He told Reuters the product, called Emdogain, would be launched at the American Academy of Periodontology's regeneration seminar in Orlando, Fla.
"We've had a few (U.S.) customers but this will be the first time we'll be out" selling the product, he said.

Emdogain is used to treat defects caused by periodontal disease, such as the loss of bone and the ligaments that hold the tooth in place in the jaw. It is a biological product and is designed to replace mechanical treatments now available.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved its use last year. It has also been authorized in Europe.

The company had a net loss last year of $5.1 million, or $0.71 per American Depositary Receipt (ADR). Hammargren said Biora did not expect to see strong U.S. sales this year despite the Emdogain launch.
"1997 is very much a startup year," he said, adding that periodontologists needed at least six months to see results from Emdogain.
Hammargren would not predict potential sales or income, but said he considered analysts' estimates, including those from Morgan Stanley, reasonable.

Analysts Duncan Moore and Paul Brooke started coverage of Biora last week with a rating of strong buy. They estimated a loss of $15.1 million this year, rising to a profit of $2.2 million in 1999 and $38 million in 2002.
Each treatment costs about $150 and Moore and Brooke estimated Emdogain's potential worldwide market at $200 million a year.

Biora has expanded its sales and marketing network in Europe and the United States and has entered into a marketing agreement with Japan's Seikagaku Corp. The number of Biora employees has risen to 58 from 12 a year ago.
Biora ADRs were off 1/4 to 20-3/4 in moderate early afternoon trade.
